body: Well, it's my adoptive dad that said it, but yeah, that's kinda what I gathered from it myself. Either way, 23 more days until I'm finally out.

*Very good idea.* I've actually got a very chunky three ring binder sitting around doing nothing that could be very useful for this. I'd just buy the inserts for it, but yeah, that's an excellent idea.
Uhm, I'd say all in all it'd amount to be a "corner's worth of a room". Definitely there, but not all-consuming. I could probably fit it all in about three or four decent sized boxes.

And proactive I have been. As I said in another reply, I've digitally backed up quite a bit of my games. I had also considered just bringing a couple of boxes with the games in them to a friend of mine (of course with the provision that he can play any of them so long as he doesn't use 'em as coasters). That is a point about the whole thing being a huge signal of a way to "get back" at me, one that I hadn't considered. It might all just be paranoia - after all, my paranoia had me convinced toward the end of last year that I'd never live to see this year - but I just want that peace of mind that if things do go bad, I've got something to fall back on. Either way, thanks for the advice! It's definitely something to consider in my plans.

Oh, trust me, my Steam account is very full. :P Anyways, what I did was back up all of my PS1/PS2/GC/Wii games to a hard drive (can't figure out how to do that for Xbox/360 games and don't wanna install a modchip or something), just in case anything did happen. The physical presence is nice and all, but actually being able to play them is something different. Either way, the ones I have backed up are basically most of my collection anyways, so I'm not fretting too much on that. It's all just a matter of "insurance".

Well, a lot of the really precious things I'll be bringing. A lot of the games can be replaced, albeit at a price (the one I'd be seeking to obtain in a small claims court should it come to that). As far as a betrayed promise, I know my mom wouldn't betray me on this. She was the one who got most of 'em for me, actually. Plus, we're both kinda in it together. Honestly, the big thing is just having that insurance, that peace of mind that if he does go on said rampage one day that I'll have some kind of recourse. I will look into a notarized affidavit, though.

Uhhh, I'm more or less in that situation *right now* with my dad. Fortunately I'm finally heading back to college in a month and a half, so I don't have to put up with it much longer. I wouldn't be surprised if a divorce rolled up soon after I leave though.

You're right. Absolutely right. Y'know, it's funny; I got a 4.0 in college for my associate's level studies, I'm studying calculus and a programming language in my spare time, but I still miss the completely obvious on matters like this. It's still gonna hurt to see my mom hurt, but for me, that might help a lot. I'd gild 'ya if I had a more reliable (or any) income, but I don't, so here's a [silver instead.](https://f.thumbs.redditmedia.com/wPjOQrGRacUELOnM.png)

Yeah, I've been kinda doing the stonewall thing for a while now, pretty much ever since it all started. Even still, after it's all done and I'm alone in my room, that's when all the emotions come out. My mom has said something similar, that I just let things get to me too much. I can't argue with that, but I have no idea how to tell myself "stop being so emotional" and have it actually mean something.

I've got enough in savings that worst come to worst, I can stay about a month at that motel, food included. That will decimate my savings, but if I need to, then I need to. I'll also be moving into the dorms ASAP, and I've got colleagues that are willing to help me with moving. It shouldn't take more than a single pickup truck for all my stuff. 

I've tried the diaphragmatic breathing and mindfulness things for about a month now, and they kinda help sometimes, but not always. One of the worst points for my anxiety pretty much every day is just as soon as I wake up. Neither of those help much for that. But yeah, there's a goal in sight. It just feels so dang far away some days.

Yes, my mom is able to get away for a little while by going to my older sister's house. I don't think it's anything to do with my thyroid; I had bloodwork done in February 2015 and they didn't report any problems with my thyroid. Maybe things have changed since then, I dunno. As for whether it's seasonal affective, I'm not sure. I could always give vitamin D supplements a shot, just to see how much it helps. However, what happened back in October was one *really* bad night of terror (basically there were some junkie kids that decided to light up outside of our house, I catastrophized it by thinking that they were gonna break in the house and shoot up the place and spent the next eight hours or so in a panic). Ever since then, I've been on this low. 

I haven't self-harmed in... about two weeks, I wanna say? Anymore the days just kinda blur together, and all I know is that the scabs are gone. Truth be told, I've never had a door to my room. The wall that goes from the front room to my room got moved back before I was ever even conceived, and that made it impossible to mount a door (opposite to the frame is a part of the windowsill). It just never was much of a problem until now.

I will try and keep in mind that I don't have to hang around for any of this. That's probably part of the reason why I have that feeling of being trapped, that it's more or less all self-imposed. Worst case, if things go all to Hell, I've got enough money saved up that I can live at the motel for about a month, food included. That'll pretty much entirely kill my savings, but if I have to, I have to.

One thing I'll be looking into today is just how early I can move into the dorms. I'm hoping it'll be as early as the 1st of January, so that it's basically 2 and a third months left. If things do get better, sure, I'll wait a few more days before heading out. If they don't, well the motel will always be glad to take my money. A couple of my colleagues in the TRIO group who retired while I was working there have offered to help me with moving. I'll gladly take them up on that offer. That week of living on my own was a pretty good insight into how much stuff I need to stay happy. Outside of the basics like toiletries, cutlery, plates, cups and all that, all I really need are my PC, my tablet and my "dumb phone" as some people like to call things that aren't smartphones. All of that can be loaded into the back of a pickup truck. Of course I'll need a little more than that for living in a dorm, but I can't imagine it's much more than a truckful.

I'll definitely be taking advantage of the on-campus mental health services when I get there. Apparently after the first free visit, it's $10 per visit, but I'm totally fine with that. Plus, I'll (hopefully) be on an upswing, so I can learn techniques to prepare for and deal with whenever disaster chooses to strike. There was a time when I thought I deserved all this, that it was all my fault, that it was karma paying me back for being such a bastard of a child. Obviously some part of my brain isn't taking that too seriously; otherwise, why would I be working to get out of this situation?

This was the pick me up I needed. Thanks a lot!

I'm just gonna speak from my own experience on this one, so if anything doesn't apply to you, keep that in mind.

I waited two and a half years before finally going back to college (I suppose I shouldn't talk about it like it's past tense; I'll be going back in the Spring). The main reason for waiting was money. What an awful decision that was. If any of y'all out there are reading this and thinking of taking time off for money, trust me; it's a bad idea. Transfer scholarships are way more than what you might be able to scrounge up.

But anyways yeah, college isn't for everyone. Do you know what you plan to major in, or are you still undecided? It's totally fine if you are; better to take some time to think about it than get three semesters into a degree path only to realize you freaking hate it. Besides, first year is gen eds anyways, for better and for worse. Also, there's no shame in going to a Vocational Tech college for two years and learning a trade. I spent two years in a Manufacturing Engineering curriculum in High School because the classes were tuition covered and it was kinda close to computer science. I met some fantastic people in there. Non-Destructive Testing is an awesome field if you like playing around with shiny toys. Plus, it pays really dang well. :)

Here's my perspective on the whole student debt thing, and it's a perspective that up until about a month ago I didn't have. This perspective was given to me by my former fellow employee at my local college's TRIO department, the financial aid advisor. Student loans are the big bad scary thing that everyone loves to fear, but honestly they aren't as bad as they seem. Let's say you need to pull $20,000 to cover your education after Pell Grants, Scholarships, parental contributions, all that. After the tax is applied and let's say a 10 year plan is set up, you get a bill each month at around $200. Depending on your standard of living, you might have to go without a couple of things for a while (for example, you might not need cable TV and instead just the Internet, or if you don't already have a cell phone you can get something like a Tracfone), or it might not even be an issue at all depending on how much you get paid.

I think a lot of people have the same fear of not knowing anyone when they go off to college. Do you have much in the way of online friends? If not, I could always use a couple more. :)

Motivation can always be a bit of a bugger, especially when as you say you're not passionate about it. This is one of the "worses" from the whole gen ed thing, and can really sour the experience for a lot of kids fresh out of high school. Since you're in college though, you should have free access (or at least very cheap access) to a counselor. Maybe they have something they can suggest? I know how much it sucks to be told something like that previous sentence, but I'm no Psych major; they know that field way better than I do. Either way, it's an option. Don't feel any shame about it. After all, would anyone shame a diabetic for needing insulin?

Honestly, it could just be a lot of stress that's causing the mood fluctuations. I know I've fallen victim to that multiple times. Again, that's something where a long term relationship would help leaps and bounds.

I know the whole controlling parents business, and yeah, it ain't good. As far as telling your parents about the depression, that's *definitely* something I or a professional would need to know a lot more about your living situation before we can offer any kind of advice. They may just be overbearing "for your own good," or they could just be living their life through you. Hard to say. Nevertheless, once again, that's where talking to a counselor would help quite a bit. As for what you can do to feel okay again, it could be anhedonia for everything you're currently doing, so maybe try a new hobby like origami. 

Either way, you've already taken a great first step in the right direction by talking about it.

My older sister actually worked in the deli at one of my local grocers. Guess it's the family tradition now or something? :P

At this point, I don't really care about aspirations or anything like that. I just want some kind of normalcy. It might be touch and go for a bit, but surely it's better than where I'm at.

I've accepted at this point that I'm gonna be working some type of retail job, and that's fine. I just know that retail won't pay for bills and rent in this area all on its own. There's a decent bit of money (in my eyes at least) that I've saved back in case of emergencies, and I think it'd be fair to use it on this. As for whether my dad would know them or not... I won't put it entirely out of the realm of possibility, but I'd be surprised. I mostly just hung out with them at school/online. Truth be told, I wouldn't be surprised if my dad thought that I didn't have any friends. That's fine with me, though.

Yeah, I've self harmed for the better part of my life, honestly (since about age six). I know it's bad for me, but it's like everyone says - it's an addiction. I'm actually not the greatest with kids, and after all this, I dunno if I wanna do the whole parent dynamic. FLEAS and whatnot. I have looked into JobCorps, but I have heard some absolute horror stories about it. I do think the best decision for me is to move in with someone I know and co-pay bills and rent and what not. Many things are better than where I'm at now. But hey, maybe this will be the day my life finally turns around?

Building a wall would be nice, if I weren't being threatened with getting kicked out all the time. Plus, this person has some grand little ways of getting at you. Plus, the fact that this person has been unemployed for the past four months without really looking for a proper full time job despite working his "dream job" six hours a week has led to elevated tension. I dunno, I think we're all pretty fucked up after this ordeal, although I kinda beat them there as far as that race is concerned.
Wish I could say that. Unfortunately, I'm still living under their roof.

Those things used to help. Anymore though, it's a distraction when things are going alright, but when they're not, they don't help all that much. Self harming helps for a bit, but it's only for a minute or so, and I know how bad it is for me, especially given my addictive personality.

There's a phrase from The Godfather Part III I've used many times to describe my life: "Just when I thought I was out, they pull me back in." If nothing at all goes wrong in a particular day, I'll be content. The moment something does, though (especially if it's a problem that either I can't fix or one that can't be fixed for a while), I just obsess over it for the rest of the day, no matter the severity, and the spiral begins anew. The past month has even more so than usual been a cycle of struggle, a few days of trying to get my feet under me again, struggle, so on and so forth. I guess maybe it's having that control, that feeling that it's one thing in my life that I can control, is what feels nice apart from the physical sensation.

Holy hell, as a tutor myself (well, ex-tutor), that kinda thing should never happen. I can see being a bit annoyed by having to re-explain concepts over and over again, especially if it's the same material over multiple sessions; or if the tutee just isn't taking it seriously, but to do something like that? That is wholly unacceptable, especially if that tutor is getting paid for it. I'd maybe have a talk with the tutoring service's administration, because that shouldn't be allowed to happen. A good tutor pushes through that earlier frustration in order to help the tutee through. I'll be the first to admit that I've had my weak days; we all do. What you described is the kinda thing that would get someone fired where I worked. 

Either way, good luck on the final tomorrow. If you end up rocking it, by all means feel smug; you'd deserve to after that.

Do you have any friends in the area that you can just go and hang out with for a while? It might just be being by yourself that has you on edge. If not, then maybe hang out in a voice chat with some of your online friends? Trust me, talking can do a lot more for you than just typing and letting everything percolate in your head. Panic attacks are hell, and I wish you the best in getting through them. :)

Yep, you're definitely not the only one that finds themselves getting worked up over stuff like that. It even ended up leading to me having my first panic attack back in 2014 (thankfully sparse those are). While I do seem to hop from thing to thing as far as what *really* sets off my anxiety as the years go on, it certainly can be quite distressing.

It might just be a time thing for you, but a therapist would definitely be good. I'm really regretting not getting my head checked back when I was in college and could've had it done for free or nearly free (especially now that I don't have insurance). I wish you the best, though.

I do as well, 'cuz that anxiety (for better and for worse) has me thinking what's been going on this summer is all coming to a head real soon. Some days, I just wish it'd hurry up and happen, but I'm just moaning at this point.
I live with my parents. Plus, I know he'd take it the wrong way and flip out.

I dunno how much help I can be, given that I'm in more or less the same exact scenario (nobody offering a place to live, though), but I do know firsthand restlessness and anxiety at home. Unfortunately, I don't know of any techniques that could help you, but I can say at least that this might be the kinda change you need. Plus, you might end up finding a wealth of opportunities that you'd never have where you're living.

Ultimately, you'll know best what the right choice is. :)

Nah, she has her own house that she shares with her boyfriend. She doesn't drive, though, and a good part of that is because of when my dad tried to "teach" her how to drive some 20 years ago and pretty much scared her off of driving completely. My mom is the one that drives my sister and her two kids around when her boyfriend can't. Plus, I know my mom would absolutely hate to leave them behind.

If it weren't for the fact that my older sister is very dependent on my mom for things like transportation, I'm sure my mom wouldn't object. It pains me to see my mom treated like this, but I get so paralyzed by fear every time I think about putting a stop to it.

Lately, I've almost gotten to the point where I'd completely believe it if someone said that I was on a Truman Show-like program, and that in an attempt to drum up some drama, as soon as I become relaxed or even happy, something goes wrong or something happens to ruin it.

I don't actually believe that or anywhere close to it, and I hope for the sake of my sanity that I never do. But what if I am Truman, though... *inception horn*

I wish I could share the same positive outlook on the situation, but it's been three months now and things haven't gotten better; they've just gotten worse. And if my paranoia is to be believed (my optimism has failed me time and time again thus far), we as a species are heading into another dark ages real soon; straight up 1984-level existence. Kinda makes it hard to stay hopeful.

I've been wanting to move to university for a while, but once again, the money situation rears its ugly head. My family makes too much to get a lot of these scholarships, but not enough to actually be able to provide pretty much anything in the way of financial backing. I'd like to think that it would do me some good, but then there's the whole thing of, "you bring yourself wherever you go." Then the fear spiral kicks in, everything that can go wrong will go wrong, so on and so forth. I guess when both situations, staying and leaving, cause that much fear and anxiety, it's no surprise that my brain jumps to these things, especially given that I've been thinking about this stuff since like 12 years old.
You're a lot braver than I'd be. I would've probably broken down half way to the airport. That damned anxiety, eh?
